note: Joe (2026-10-01): the small two-storey cream-and-brick shop with a red-orange awning east of Ted Drewes, in Maplewood, becomes the St. Louis Bread Co. at 6607 Chippewa, drawn after Joe's Street View reference (art/references/local/places/st-louis-bread-co/exterior-street-view.png, local only): a one-storey tan brick corner building with a flat roof, a dark standing-seam canopy wrapping the corner, arched windows, a patio with green umbrellas behind wooden screens and pink shrubs along the front, with one clear front door, the door of the bread-co interior. Codex drew the building six times from the fixes below with the photograph as reference 3 (a to c on a 288 x 192 tile, d to f on this one); every attempt drew it well and none held the tile's registration: a, b, c and e were rejected for drift, and d and f, which passed, drew it larger than the lot so the mask cut its patio and roof. So the tile is placed by hand (the README's third way): the shop, its tables, the bush west of it and the small tree east of it are cleared to the lot's own paving and lawn, and attempt a's building, cut out along its outline, is pasted at 0.143 native px per attempt px, its back roof corner at native 385, 479.5. The same cut-out is the decal bread-co-building.png, and the sign's lettering the decal bread-co-sign.svg (decals.json). Ted Drewes, the road, the small tree north-east of the shop and the big foreground tree are outside the mask.

fixes: Outline (Maplewood, just east of the white ice-cream stand with the yellow striped awning): a small two-storey cream-and-brick shop with a red-orange awning and scribbled cafe tables in front. Replace it with a St. Louis Bread Co. bakery-cafe drawn after reference 3, a photograph of the real building, in this map's own flat vector style, camera, scale and light. It is ONE storey, lower and wider than the old shop: a tan brick box (warm light brick, about #D7A070, with a slightly darker shaded side) with a flat roof and a thin pale stone coping, seen exactly as every other building in the tile is seen: its long front wall faces the viewer and its shorter right side wall recedes up to the right. A dark slate-grey standing-seam metal canopy with a sloped top runs along both visible walls about halfway up and wraps the front right corner in one piece. Under the canopy the brick walls carry a row of dark arched windows with thin black frames, and in the middle of the front wall is ONE clear entrance: a glass double door in a dark frame, taller than the windows, with a short cream walk leading from it straight down to the paving. Above the canopy the front wall has a tall plain brick parapet carrying one wide olive-green rectangular sign panel (about #6F7F2B), completely blank: no lettering, no logo, no marks on it. The side wall's parapet carries a second, smaller blank olive-green panel. Against the building's left end stands a small patio on the cream paving: two round lime-green umbrellas over small tables, behind two low honey-coloured slatted wooden screens. Along the foot of the front wall, either side of the door, low round shrubs with pink blossoms and green leaves.

The building stands on the old shop's spot, its back right corner where the old one's was; it may reach a little further left and forward than the old shop, but stays wholly inside the outline with paving or lawn all round it. It stands flat on the cream paving with a soft shadow at its right, nothing floating, every wall meeting the ground in a clean straight line. Remove the old cafe tables and the old awning completely. Keep the small green bush behind the building's back left corner, and draw one small round tree, whole, on the lawn at the building's right. The lawn at the right stays the lawn's own flat green and the paving in front stays cream paving that joins the footpaths around it without a seam.
